title: rosa canina subsp. vulgaris
intro: Rosa canina subsp. vulgaris, commonly known as the common wild rose, is a subspecies of the Rosa canina plant that is native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa. The plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal and therapeutic properties, offering numerous health benefits including reducing inflammation, improving cardiovascular health, and supporting digestive well-being. The therapeutic actions of Rosa canina subsp. vulgaris include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which contribute to its effectiveness in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions and health benefits.
